CSE - Script Path & Search Paths.vi

Owning Palette: CSE Script Processor

The VI associates a parsed script with both a file path of the source script and a set of search directory paths. These paths are used to find target script files when the given script calls other scripts using relative paths.

Details

Click the parameters for more information

 

CSE RefNum is a reference number for a CSE instance that contains a parsed CSE script. CSE - Parse Script.vi returns a value that can be wired directly to this terminal.
script file path specifies a file path to be associated with the given parsed script if action control is equal to save.
search paths specifies an array of search directory paths to be associated with the given parsed script if action control is equal to save.
error in describes error conditions that occur before this VI runs. This input provides standard error in functionality.
status indicates error status.
code contains error code.
source contains additional error information.
action specifies an opetations to perform:

0getThe VI returns a script file path and array of search paths associated with the parsed script.
1saveThe VI associates script file path and search paths with the specified CSE instance context.
dup CSE RefNum is a flow-through parameter with the same value as CSE RefNum.
script file path out returns a path associated with the given parsed script.
search paths out returns a path associated with the given parsed script.
error out contains error information. This output provides standard error out functionality.
status indicates error status.
code contains error code.
source contains additional error information.

 

CSE - Script Path & Search Paths.vi - details

If any input path is relative, the VI converts it to the absolute path based on a directory path where the top-level VI in its call chain resides. If the top-level VI resides in a library or an executable program, an actual directory path is taken for the basis.
